title: A bat can change the speed and the direction of a pitched ball
summary: OpenStax Physics uses a pitched ball struck by a bat as an example of an outside force changing speed and direction.
body: OpenStax Physics, opening Newton's second law, says a change in motion is caused by an external force. The instance is a pitched ball that changes speed and direction when a bat hits it. A change in motion, the section says, is a change in velocity: speed, direction, or both. Only a nonzero net external force produces that change, and the page calls the change an acceleration. The bat is an illustration. The page does not time a swing.

sources.title: OpenStax Physics, 4.3 Newton's Second Law of Motion
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Physics web page (/books/physics/), CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the pitched-ball and bat example and the statement that a nonzero net external force causes acceleration.
